title: Progress at the expense of accountability: why the European Commission's approach to DMA compromise falls short
bib_title: Progress at the expense of accountability: why the Commission's approach to DMA compromise falls short
key_claim: The post argues that the Commission's negotiated compromises with gatekeepers, including Meta's pay-or-consent model and Apple's August 2026 app changes, trade accountability for speed and foreclose judicial and social scrutiny.
frame_summary: Argues DMA enforcement is falling short because the Commission prefers closed-door agreements with gatekeepers over contestable decisions, which forecloses third-party redress.
verbatim_quote: In sum, the enforcer signals a clear predilection for behind-closed-doors agreements with gatekeepers to steer clear of accountability, both judicially and socially.

title: The revised EU Product Liability Directive: state of play across EU member states and evolving risk landscape
bib_title: The revised EU Product Liability Directive: state of play across EU member states and the evolving risk landscape
key_claim: The revised Product Liability Directive brings software and AI-driven technologies clearly within no-fault liability and must be transposed by 9 December 2026; as of June 2026 Hungary alone had adopted its law and draft bills had been published in ten member states.
frame_summary: Argues that a maximum-harmonisation directive is producing divergent national regimes, so the practical exposure for software and AI-enabled products is unpredictable rather than uniform.
cluster: Deadlines bind before national laws arrive
verbatim_quote: The EU PLD represents a fundamental shift in Europe's product liability regime, particularly with regard to perceived gaps in the areas of digital products, software, and AI-driven technologies.
verbatim_list: Hungary is the only Member State that has already adopted the EU PLD transposition legislation.

In 2024, the European Union published the revised Product Liability Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2853; "EU PLD"), which must be transposed into the national laws of all EU Member States by December 9, 2026.
